title: Interactive On-Net Operator (MGySgt to Pvt) NMOS (1721, 1799, 2629, 2651, 2659), DC I
raw_text:
2. MOS 1712, Interactive On-Net Operator (MGySgt to Pvt) NMOS (1721, 1799,
2629, 2651, 2659), DC I

    a. Summary. This NMOS requires advanced cyberspace operations
training. Interactive On-Net Operators are involved in all facets of
planning and delivering cyberspace effects to achieve tactical, operational,
and strategic objectives. The Interactive On-Net Operator must be an expert
with computer hardware and software programs to include network operating
systems. The duties for MOS 1712 encompass cyberspace operations,
intelligence operations, and information operations planning support to
develop situational awareness within the cyberspace environment. Interactive
On-Net Operators are technical experts in offensive cyberspace operations.
The duties for MOS 1712 increase with experience in multiple disciplines to
encompass developing new techniques and methods, technical leadership, and
serving as the subject matter expert for tools, techniques, and procedures.

    b. Prerequisites. Must be currently assigned to one of the following
PMOSs 1721, 1799, 2629, 2651, or 2659.

       c.    Requirements

        (1) Complete training and certification requirements as determined by
apprentice level national security agency or senior level United States Cyber
Command standards.

        (2) MOS 1712 assigned upon approval of the Director, Information
Maneuver Division.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to NAVMC
3500.124A, Information Maneuver Training and Readiness Manual.

    e.       Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.    Related Military Skill

             (1) Offensive Cyberspace Warfare Officer, 1710.

             (2) Exploitation Analyst, 1713.

             (3) Cyberspace Warfare Operator, 1721.



                                         3-119                        Enclosure (1)
 3118                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



            (4) Cyberspace Warfare Chief, 1799.

The Information Maneuver Occupational Field integrates information capability areas and the military occupational specialties (MOS) of cyberspace, space, electromagnetic warfare, civil affairs, and psychological operations into a single OCCFLD. Marines from these disciplines utilize their exquisite talents, knowledge, skills, and abilities to generate, preserve, and apply informational power against a relevant actor in order to increase or protect competitive advantage or combat power potential within all domains of the operating environment. Duty assignments include Marine Corps Forces Cyberspace Command, Marine Corps Forces Space Command, Marine Corps Information Command, Marine Cryptologic Support Battalion, Marine Corps Information Operations Center, MEF information groups, HQMC, MARFORs, joint organizations, and staff sections at all levels of the MAGTF.

2. MOS 1712, Interactive On-Net Operator (MGySgt to Pvt) NMOS (1721, 1799, 2629, 2651, 2659), DC I a. Summary. This NMOS requires advanced cyberspace operations training. Interactive On-Net Operators are involved in all facets of planning and delivering cyberspace effects to achieve tactical, operational, and strategic objectives. The Interactive On-Net Operator must be an expert with computer hardware and software programs to include network operating systems. The duties for MOS 1712 encompass cyberspace operations, intelligence operations, and information operations planning support to develop situational awareness within the cyberspace environment. Interactive On-Net Operators are technical experts in offensive cyberspace operations. The duties for MOS 1712 increase with experience in multiple disciplines to encompass developing new techniques and methods, technical leadership, and serving as the subject matter expert for tools, techniques, and procedures. b. Prerequisites. Must be currently assigned to one of the following PMOSs 1721, 1799, 2629, 2651, or 2659. c. Requirements (1) Complete training and certification requirements as determined by apprentice level national security agency or senior level United States Cyber Command standards. (2) MOS 1712 assigned upon approval of the Director, Information Maneuver Division. d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to NAVMC 3500.124A, Information Maneuver Training and Readiness Manual.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
